subject: sports-science
intro: Sports science leads into the professions built around physical performance — coaching, fitness training, clinical exercise work and the rehabilitation of injured bodies.

roles.title: Athletic Trainers
roles.what: Evaluate and treat musculoskeletal injuries and illnesses in athletes and active people, providing preventive, therapeutic, emergency and rehabilitative care on the field and in clinics.
roles.where: The anatomy and physiology unit — skeletal and muscular systems, circulation and respiration — underpins injury evaluation, while the principles of training and overload topic explains how overuse injuries are prevented in the first place.

roles.title: Exercise Physiologists
roles.what: Assess, plan and implement fitness programs using exercise to improve cardiorespiratory function, body composition, muscular strength, muscular endurance and flexibility, often for patients with chronic conditions.
roles.where: Energy supply and the effects of exercise on the body, the components of fitness, test protocols and the methods of training topic are precisely the knowledge base a clinical exercise physiologist applies to every programme.

roles.title: Exercise Trainers and Group Fitness Instructors
roles.what: Instruct or coach groups and individuals in exercise for personal fitness, demonstrating correct technique and form, observing participants and explaining the corrective measures needed to improve.
roles.where: The Health, fitness and training unit maps directly onto the job: methods of training, overload principles, diet and energy sources, and the fitness-testing protocols used to track a client's progress.

roles.title: Coaches and Scouts
roles.what: Instruct or coach individuals and teams in the fundamentals of a sport for competition, demonstrate techniques, and evaluate athletes' strengths and weaknesses to improve performance or assess recruits.
roles.where: The skill acquisition and psychology unit is the coach's toolkit: skill classification, the information processing model, feedback, goal setting, motivation and arousal — all applied when preparing performers for competition.

roles.title: Physical Therapists
roles.what: Assess, plan and participate in rehabilitative programmes that improve mobility, relieve pain, build strength and correct disabling conditions resulting from disease or injury.
roles.where: The skeletal and muscular system topics and the simple biomechanics unit give the movement vocabulary rehabilitation rests on, and the fitness-testing topics transfer directly to measuring a patient's recovery.
